clue.text: Record achieved by Beckett

parts.note: reads like a sporting record set by someone called Beckett, but it means the play by Samuel Beckett in which an old man listens to tape recordings of his younger self

explanation.surface: An athlete named Beckett has set a new record.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's one-act play centres on a spool of recorded tape, so the record is literally a recording and the title is his.

clue.text: No man should be confused recalling David's first-born

indicators.note: being confused means the letters of the words no man get jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a man ought to be muddled when thinking back about King David's eldest son.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Amnon son of Ahinoam was the eldest son of King David.

clue.text: Pet's nursery accessory provided by Maurice baring (5)

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet; the possessive gives the S
a cradle is a baby's rocking bed in the nursery

explanation.surface: A pet animal's piece of nursery furniture was supplied by a man named Maurice who was stripping something bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baring' looks like a verb, but it is the novelist Maurice Baring, whose 1925 novel bears this title. The stray '(5)' is a printing leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the novel by Maurice Baring, which is also the name of a string game played between two pairs of hands.

clue.text: Her love struck a chord which spanned an octave

definitions.text: Her love struck a chord which spanned an octave

parts.words: Her love struck a chord which spanned an octave
parts.note: reads as music, a wide chord across eight notes, but the heroine of a Stendhal novel loved a man called Octave

explanation.surface: A woman's love affair moved someone like a pianist playing a wide chord.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stendhal's first novel the heroine loves her cousin Octave de Malivert, so 'an octave' is the man, not the musical interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal's 1827 novel is named for its heroine, whose beloved is Octave de Malivert.

clue.text: Its hero earlier seen as artistic young man

definitions.text: Its hero earlier seen as artistic young man

parts.words: Its hero earlier seen as artistic young man
parts.note: the Joyce novel whose central young man, Stephen Dedalus, appeared before in A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

explanation.surface: A book's hero had previously appeared as an arty youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints ULYYSES, a slip for the Joyce novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's 1922 novel brings back Stephen Dedalus, hero of his earlier Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.

clue.text: Dead language encountered in train carriage

indicators.note: the answer is met with inside the run of letters of the words train carriage

explanation.surface: Someone overheard a dead language spoken in a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire's people spoke a tongue no longer used in its imperial form, so the name stands for that dead language in crosswords.

clue.text: Peerless quality of Mrs Bagnet (Bleak House)

definitions.text: Peerless quality of Mrs Bagnet (Bleak House)

parts.words: Peerless quality of Mrs Bagnet (Bleak House)
parts.note: a word meaning without equal, which is how Mrs Bagnet, the soldier's wife in Dickens's Bleak House, is praised

explanation.surface: A question about the unmatched virtue of a Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having no equal, the matchless excellence Dickens gives the good Mrs Bagnet.

clue.text: Storyteller's sister described as relative replacement typist last Friday (4, )

parts.note: an aunt is a family relative
a temp is a temporary office worker standing in for a regular typist

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Friday

explanation.surface: A storyteller's sister is described as a relative who covered for the typist at the end of last week.
explanation.walkthrough: The storyteller is Uncle Remus, in whose tales she appears; the stray '(4, )' is a printing leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: A character among the old women in Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories, companion to the narrator.

clue.text: Able to show part of Pound

parts.note: to be able is to can, as in I can
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is able to display a portion of a pound of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money or weight but is the poet Ezra Pound, whose long poem is made of numbered sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound's epic The Cantos is built of sections each called by this name.

clue.text: Godlike acute anxiety ()

definitions.meaning: relating to the Greek god Pan, the adjective's old sense

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means belonging to the god Pan, and as a noun it is the sudden terror once blamed on him.

clue.text: It's hard lines he wrote

parts.note: sounds like sympathy for bad luck, but Hard Lines was the first verse collection of the American comic poet Ogden

explanation.surface: Someone commiserates with a writer over his bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden of that surname published his first book of light verse, Hard Lines, in 1931.

clue.text: Republican traitor returns in Lewis book

indicators.note: returning means the letters for Republican and traitor are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is slang for a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A Republican turncoat comes back in a book about a man called Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyndham Lewis's first novel, published in 1918, about an English artist in Paris.

clue.text: Corrupt (but guardedly so? )

parts.note: corrupt in the way the Roman emperors' bodyguard was notoriously venal, the guard pun on guardedly

explanation.surface: A cautious hint that something is corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means venal or corrupt, after the bribable imperial guard of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Author of book of Proverbs

parts.note: not the biblical book but a medieval English poet who wrote a set of verses titled Proverbs

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote the Book of Proverbs in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: John of that name, the fifteenth-century monk poet of Bury St Edmunds, wrote moral verses called Proverbs.

clue.text: Filmed reportage featuring medical man at university play

parts.note: doc is informal for a doctor
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A news film shows a doctor at a university theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: A film that dramatises real events, a blend of documentary and drama.

clue.text: Like Breton's mode of thought, not quite sure, but actual

indicators.note: not quite means the word sure stops short of its last letter

parts.note: real means actual

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure what the French writer Breton thought but knows it was genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: Breton is André Breton, author of the Surrealist Manifesto, not a person from Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: André Breton founded the movement whose dreamlike thought this adjective describes.

clue.text: "Although her body die, her fame survives, / A —— bird, ages of lives." (Samson Agonistes)

definitions.text: "Although her body die, her fame survives, / A —— bird, ages of lives." (Samson Agonistes)

parts.words: "Although her body die, her fame survives, / A —— bird, ages of lives." (Samson Agonistes)
parts.note: a fill-in from Milton describing the phoenix, which lives for an age before being reborn

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton about the phoenix with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Milton the word carries its old sense of lasting for an age or centuries, apt for the long-lived phoenix.

clue.text: Snubs concerning devotees

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
buffs are enthusiasts or devotees

explanation.surface: An account of slights about some keen fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean curt rejections or brush-offs.

clue.text: Return of the 1960s maverick fashion house in Jewish month

explanation.surface: A celebrated sixties boutique comes back during a month in the Jewish calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The early biblical name for the first month of the Hebrew year, later called Nisan.

clue.text: Presumably clean-shaven philosopher ()

parts.note: a joke on the medieval thinker whose principle of economy is called a razor

explanation.surface: A guess that some philosopher never had a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: William of this English village gave his name to the razor, the principle of cutting needless assumptions.

clue.text: Short story from Tartarin de Tarascon (tedious, though)

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run spanning Tarascon tedious

explanation.surface: A short story taken from Daudet's comic Tartarin de Tarascon, though it is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a tale, used in English for a short story.

clue.text: Poet, when penniless, becomes another

explanation.surface: A poor poet turns into someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope without a P leaves Poe, Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander of this surname was the leading English poet of the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Culminating work of nineteen-year-old drop-out

parts.note: the last great poem of Rimbaud, written at nineteen before he gave up poetry altogether
